items.briefing:
Scammers are increasingly targeting Australians with two fast-growing attack methods: "device code phishing" — where you're tricked into approving access to your accounts through a fake login prompt — and voice phishing (vishing) calls impersonating trusted sources. Both have surged dramatically in 2026. Separately, a report highlights that rapid fintech growth in Australia is creating security gaps, so staff using financial apps or platforms should be cautious about the permissions they grant and the data they share.

**Practical tip:** If you receive an unexpected call or message asking you to approve a login or enter a code, stop and verify through an official channel before doing anything.

featured.title: Device Code Phishing Up 1,500% in 2026; Vishing Doubles
featured.quote: Device code phishing surge exposes Australian organisations to rapidly evolving social engineering threats.
